headline: Plasmid, phage and genomic-context tools refine resolution of gut and pathogen bacterial ecology
label: Gut Mobile Element Genomics
summary: New preprints and a TwinsUK phageome study pair mobile element analyses with taxonomic, transmission, spatial and eukaryote-detection tools for microbiome data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving mobile genetic elements and genomic context in gut-associated and pathogenic bacteria. The ETEC preprint reports contrasting plasmid-host associations shaping colonization factor distribution. The TwinsUK study builds a 116,740-vOTU phage catalogue from 1,069 gut metagenomes and links phage genomic variation to bacterial species and microbial metabolites. Adjacent tools address context rather than mobile elements directly: Robust Cluster Typing assigns genomes to species-level groups using ribosomal proteins, demonstrated on Campylobacter; SNP2Cluster-Py provides context-aware core SNP clustering, tested on Klebsiella and pneumococcal datasets; MiSA detects disease-associated spatial dysbiosis in HiPR-FISH images; and metaEukaryome detects eukaryotic bycatch in 75,727 metagenomes via mitochondrial and plastid sequences.
